title: Optimal packings of one to seven unit squares in a disk
abstract: For n = 1, …, 7: the least radius of a closed disk holding n unit squares with disjoint interiors, each placed and rotated freely, and every packing that attains it. The radii are √2/2, √5/2, 5√17/16, √2, √(5/2), √q* ≈ 1.68854 and √13/2, where q* is a quartic irrational. Up to rotation about the disk centre and relabelling, the optimal packing is unique for n ≤ 6: the square, the 2 × 1 rectangle, the T, the 2 × 2 block, the plus, and for six squares a central square with four neighbours, two of them pushed along its sides, and a sixth square turned by π/4 between those two. For n = 7 the optimal packings form a three-parameter family: two columns of two squares and, between them, a column of three whose heights vary independently, at least 1 apart and within √3 − 1/2 of the disk centre. The proofs for three to six squares bound the arcs the squares occupy on a small circle about the disk centre. For six squares this finds the square that contains the disk centre; five fixed points label the others, and a weighted sum of separating inequalities, with estimates uniform in the angles of the squares, forces the optimal radius. For seven squares, each square avoiding the disk centre gets a direction from it, and in the optimal disk two disjoint such squares get directions at least π/3 apart. We found no earlier proof for five, six or seven squares, and no exact one for three, where a computer-assisted enclosure of the radius and the optimal arrangements was known. Four squares, uniqueness included, were settled by hand in 2026, by the same idea as here.
